experiment_ids.note: KamLAND-Zen suspends a xenon-loaded inner balloon 'at the center of the KamLAND detector' (arXiv:1211.3863); it has no separate detector record in the Atlas, and the KamLAND-Zen experiment references this detector:kamland id directly.

intervals.label: reactor-antineutrino data taking
intervals.note: Start is January 2002 at month precision: arXiv:hep-ex/0405074 (Motoki et al., Tohoku Research Center for Neutrino Science) says 'In January 22, 2002, KamLAND started the data-taking', while the KamLAND proceedings arXiv:hep-ex/0405001 (Hatakeyama, for the KamLAND Collaboration) says KamLAND 'started operation on January 21st 2002', so the day is not fixed here. The 2026 collaboration paper (arXiv:2606.29381, v2 of 21 Oct 2026) says "KamLAND began data taking in March 2002 and ended data taking in August 2024.", and the first-results exposure began on 4 March 2002 (arXiv:hep-ex/0212021); this record does not resolve the January/March difference. The end (2024-08-27) comes from the KamLAND collaboration paper quoted above; the TAUP 2025 slides give the day: "Last physics run on August 27th 2024".
intervals.quote: In January 22, 2002, KamLAND started the data-taking.

end.note: Q-EYES 2025 slide: "Installation of new PMTs starting in autumn 2026 / Filling with LS starting in summer 2027 / Restart of DAQ in spring 2028"; TAUP 2025 slide: "KamLAND2 dismantling & constrution ongoing -> expected launch in 2028!".

intervals.label: KamLAND2 upgrade: detector dismantling and rebuilding (no data taking)
intervals.note: Day from the TAUP 2025 slide "Last physics run on August 27th 2024 -> dismantling of detector ongoing"; month confirmed by the collaboration paper. The restart date is a plan from December 2025 and the slide chain ends with "KamLAND2-Zen will start in FY2028-2029??" (question marks on the slide).

name: KamLAND detector
notes: `detector:kamland` is the id that KamLAND-Zen references: KamLAND-Zen loads a xenon-doped mini-balloon inside this same liquid-scintillator volume. This detector record describes KamLAND's own reactor-antineutrino configuration only; KamLAND-Zen's own specs and intervals are not recorded here.

Structural specs (target mass, PMT count) are quoted from the KamLAND first-results paper (arXiv:hep-ex/0212021) and the collaboration's 2026 full-dataset paper (arXiv:2606.29381); no official KamLAND detector page was reachable (the 'About KamLAND' sub-page returned 404 on every URL tried). The veto mass and containment vessel in `technology` rest on the first-results paper.

placements.note: Placement start is the January 2002 start of data taking at month precision (see the interval note on the January/March difference); the site coordinates are themselves only campus-grade/approximate (see site:kamioka-kamland), so confidence is kept approximate.
placements.quote: In January 22, 2002, KamLAND started the data-taking.

pmt_count.note: Stated outright by the KamLAND first-results paper (1,325 17-inch plus 554 20-inch PMTs; the 2026 collaboration paper gives the same two counts).
pmt_count.quote: An array of 1,879 photomultiplier tubes (PMTs), mounted on the inner surface of the containment vessel, completes the inner detector (ID) system.

target_mass.locator: arXiv:2606.29381, Sec. II (KamLAND Detector and Dataset)
target_mass.note: The KamLAND collaboration states 1 kton of liquid scintillator in the inner detector (a nominal, rounded figure, hence ~1000 t).
target_mass.quote: The ID contained 1 kton of LS enclosed in a 13-m-diameter nylon/EVOH (ethylene-vinyl alcohol copolymer) balloon, which was supported by non-scintillating buffer oil.

summary.plain: A giant balloon of clear liquid inside a mine in Japan, watched by nearly 1,900 light sensors, that catches antineutrinos from nuclear reactors across the country. A xenon-loaded inner balloon suspended at its centre (KamLAND-Zen) uses the same detector to search for a different rare process.
summary.technical: ~1000 t liquid-scintillator antineutrino detector in an 18 m diameter vessel with 1,879 PMTs, surrounded by a water-Cherenkov muon veto, in the old Kamiokande cavity of the Kamioka mine; operating since January 2002.

technology.note: Configuration as described in the KamLAND first-results paper (arXiv:hep-ex/0212021, Phys. Rev. Lett. 90, 021802): 13 m balloon, 18 m containment vessel, 1,879 PMTs, 3.2 kton water-Cherenkov outer detector. The balloon is 13 m; the 18 m sphere is the stainless-steel containment vessel. KamLAND-Zen reuses this same detector volume with a different central balloon/isotope load.
technology.quote: 1 kton of ultra-pure LS contained in a 13-m-diameter spherical balloon ... between the balloon and an 18-m-diameter spherical stainless-steel containment vessel ... The containment vessel is surrounded by a 3.2 kton water-Cherenkov detector
technology.value: Liquid-scintillator antineutrino detector: 1 kton of liquid scintillator in a 13-m-diameter spherical balloon, with an oil buffer between the balloon and an 18-m-diameter spherical stainless-steel containment vessel lined with 1,879 photomultiplier tubes, surrounded by a 3.2 kton water-Cherenkov outer detector that tags cosmic-ray muons
